FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 4) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Renewable Energy Sources Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division 
Council. 


This standard has five parts under general title Concentrated solar thermal — Specification. Other parts in this 
series are: 

Part 1 Paraboloid dish concentrator 

Part 2 Scheffler concentrator 

Part3 Parabolic trough concentrator 

Part5 Test methods 


The relevant SI units and corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance:

The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result ofa test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16648 (Part 4) : 2018 


Indian Standard 


CONCENTRATED SOLAR THERMAL — SPECIFICATION 
PART 4 NON-IMAGING CONCENTRATOR 


1 SCOPE 


This standard (Part 4) specifies requirements of non- 
imaging concentrator (NIC) for process heating and 
steam generation for range 60°C to 120°C. The NIC 
shall be useful for low to medium process heat 
application. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given in Annex A contain provisions, which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, 
and parties to agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the 
most recent editions of the standards. 


3 TERMONOLGY 


For purpose of this standard, following definitions shall 
apply: 


3.1 Non-Imaging Concentrator (NIC) — A solar 
collector, made up of transparent tubing (usually glass) 
within an evacuated space (partial vacuum) between 
the tube wall and the absorber. The absorber shall consist 
of an inner tube or another shape with means of removal 
of the thermal energy and shall be specially coated. The 
whole arrangement consisting of multiple tubes fitted 
with manifold plus reflector at the lower side may or 
shall not be enclosed in a box with transparent 
toughened solar glass of thickness 3 mm to 4 mm. The 
frames to hold glass should be of aluminium or steel 
section with EPDM gasket. 


3.2 Transmittance — Ratio of the radiant flux passing 
through a body to that of incident radiation. 


3.3 Tilt Angle — The angle between the vertical and 
the pyranometer axis which is identical to the angle 
between the horizontal plane and the plane of the 
detector surface. 


3.4 Absorptance — Ratio of the radiant flux 
absorption to that of incident radiation. 


3.5 Emittance — Ratio radiant existence of body to 
that of a black body at same temperature. 


3.6 Reflectance — Ratio of the radiant flux reflected 
to that of incident radiation. 


3.7 Collector, Concentrating — A solar collector that 
uses reflectors, lenses or other optical elements to 


redirect and concentrate the solar radiation passing 
through the aperture on to an absorber, the surface area 
of which is smaller than the aperture area. 


3.8 Absorber — Device within a solar collector for 
absorbing radiant energy and transferring this energy 
as heat into fluid. 


3.9 Aperture Area — Maximum projected area 
through which un-concentrated solar radiation enters 
the collector. Net area available for transmission of solar 
radiation through the outer air cover interface. 


3.10 Wind Speed — Air speed measured by 
anemometer at height of 10 m above ground level. 


3.11 Receiver — In concentrating collector, the part 
to which the solar radiation is finally directed or 
redirected and includes the absorber and any associated 
glazing through which the radiation must pass. 


3.12 Collector Tilt Angle — The lower angle between 
the aperture plane of a solar collector and the horizontal 
plane. 


3.13 Time Constant— The time required for a first order 
system to have its output change by 63.2 percent of its 
final change in output following a step change in its input. 


3.14 Symbols 


Q — Rate of energy W 

A, — Aperture area m? 

l, — Global solar irradiance W/m? 

© — Angle of incidence Degree 

a, — Temperature dependence W/m’K 
first degree heat loss coefficient

4 COMPONENTS SPECIFICATIONS 


The various components of NIC shall be as per 
specifications given below. 


IS 16648 (Part 4) : 2018 


4.1 Reflector 


Material of reflector shall be aluminium sheet with 
protective coatings for performance enhancement and 
durability. 


The reflector sheet shall have thickness in the range of 
0.3 to 0.8 mm, suitable for forming a parabola. 


The reflector shall be coated with anodizing/epoxy, 
polyester (PE), polyurethane (PU), fluorocarbon 
coating/lacquer coating for weather protection. 


a) Reflectivity shall be minimum 90 percent — 

The specimen of mirror shall be tested as per 
ASTM E 903. Measurement of spectral near 
normal cone hemispherical transmittance (or 
reflectance) are made over the spectral range 
from approximately 300 to 2 500 nm with an 
integrating sphere spectrophotometer having 
a small coal solid angle of incident flux on 
sample. 
The solar transmittance, reflectance, or 
absorptance is obtained by calculating a 
weighted average over wavelength with a 
standard solar spectral irradiance as the 
weighting function by either the weighted or 
selected ordinate method. 

b) Durability shall be minimum 10 years. The 
reflector specimen shall be subjected to the 
neutral salt spray test as per IS 9844 and 
IS 3438.The specimen shall not have any 
blisters, degradation of back coating after 
exposure of 250 h. 

c) Scratch resistance — There shall be no visible 
scratches after 100 wipes. The surface shall 
look completely unharmed. The procedure of 
the scratch test shall follow DIN 58 196 TS. 
Initially the samples shall be wiped with a felt 
cloth (diameter 10 mm) with a set force of 4.5 


ABSORBTANCE 
LAYER 


GETTAR 


N. Initial wiping shall be done ten times back 
and forth. Once the sample had passed this 
test well or showed very little signs of abrasion, 
the wiping process should be continued with 
20, 50 or 100 back and forth strokes inspecting 
after each set of wipes. 

d) Reflector shape and accuracy — 
Manufacturer shall give the dimensions of NIC 
reflector with tolerances as below. 


1) Length : in mm with +/⁄ tolerance 


2) Width : in mm with +/— tolerance

The tolerance shall be defined by manufactured in order 
to get the required optical efficiency for the specific 
design and shall be within the tolerances defined. 


4.2 Receiver Assembly 


Evacuated Receiver Tube Assembly — Receiver 
assembly shall be made of an evacuated glass tube, U 
shaped tube to remove absorbed heat and fins to transfer 
heat to the tube as per Fig. 1. 


4.2.1 Evacuated Tube 


Evacuated tube shall be as per IS 16543 suitable for 
stagnation temp of 300°C minimum. 


Absorption of coating shall be minimum 90 percent. 


Glass transmission of outer glass shall be minimum 
92 percent. 


Emissivity of absorber coating shall be maximum 
10 percent. 


The specimen of absorber tube and glass cover shall 
be tested as per ASTM E 903. Measurement of spectral

The inner absorber tube shall be selectively coated with 
aluminium nitride based material or any equivalent. 


The outer glass diameter shall be 47 mm to 70 mm. 
The outer glass thickness shall be 1.6 mm to 2.0 mm. 
4.2.1.2 Vacuum durability 

Fifty percent maximum as per IS 16543. 


Vacuum performance in the evacuated tube which is 
expressed by disappearance ratio in axial length of the 
getter mirror after interior of an evacuated tube is 
heated. 


The spark leak detector shall be used to check the air 
pressure inside the vacuum jacket. Intensity of spark 
and colour shall be used to check the vacuum standard. 


Quality test for vacuum shall be conducted by using 
electric heating rod and measuring temperature for 48 
h. The rate of disappearance should be not more than

Vacuum performance test shall be done as per IS 16543. 
4.2.1.3 Impact test 


No damage to receiver tube on impact as per procedure 
blow. 


This test shall be performed indoor. Fix the evacuated 
tube on the test frame supported by 2 V-shaped groove 
with 5 mm thick polyurethane liner with 500 mm space 
in between. A steel ball, having a mass of 120+ 10 g, 
shall be dropped from height of 450 mm oriented to 
the middle ofreceiver tube. The steel ball drops freely 
with vertical impact on the receiver tube and the receiver 
tube shall have no damage. 


4.2.2 Heat Absorber 


The U-tube shall be made of copper, stainless steel with 
thickness suitable for design pressure as per IBR code. 
The diameter and thickness of tube shall be as per 
manufacturer ’s specification. 


4.2.3 Fins 


The metal fins shall be made of aluminium or copper. 
The thickness of fins shall be decided by manufacturer 
with tolerances. 


4.3 Collector and Support Structure with Civil 
Foundation 


The collector has frame supports, evacuated tubes and 
heat removing U-tube. The frame is mounted on a stand 
which is put on foundation as shown in Fig. 2. The 
specifications of the components shall be as below.

Fic. 2 NIC SUPPORT STRUCTURE 


3 


IS 16648 (Part 4) : 2018 


4.3.1 NIC Collector/Module Frame 


The back cover shall be made of aluminium or 
galvanized iron sheet fixed on aluminium or steel frame. 
One end of receiver tube shall be fixed on to the module 
with the help of brackets and fasteners. 


Reflectors shall be glued or attached to the frame by 
weather proof glue material. The frame shall be designed 
to withstand wind speed of 47 m/s. Design should be 
as per IS 800/IS 875 (Part 3). 


Material of collector frame and support should be as 
per IS 2062, and shall be protected from corrosion with 
suitable process such as galvanization, cathode 
electrode deposition (CED) or any suitable painting 
process as per standards. The coating shall be suitable 
for life span 20 years as per IS used for the chosen 
coating process. 


4.3.2 Module Stand 


Module stand shall be made of standard steel or 
aluminium sections as per relevant codes of the sections. 


The stand shall be protected against corrosion with the 
cathode electrode deposition (CED), galvanization or 
suitable painting process for 20 years life as per IS code 
used for the chosen coating process. 


The design strength of the module, stand & foundation 
shall be in accordance with IS 875 (Part 2) and IS 875 
(Part 3). 


4.3.3 Civil Foundation 


Civil foundation shall be designed to rest on soil of 
sufficient strength or to suit the prevalent soil condition. 


The material used for civil foundation shall be cement 
and concrete. 


Strength of civil foundation shall be in accordance with 
IS 456 and allied/applied codes. 


5 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 


The shape and dimensions of the NIC may be decided 
by the manufacturer based on his design. The typical 
dimensions to be mentioned are given in Fig. 3. Typical 
system arrangement is shown in Fig. 4. 


6 ASSEMBLY AND WORKMANSHIP 


The entire assembly shall be free from surface defects. All 
sharp edges and corners shall be rounded off. The exposed 
surfaces shall be properly made corrosion resistant. 


The whole system shall be so assembled, that 
replaceable components are accessible for repair or 
replacement at site in accordance with the manufacturer 
instructions.

7.2 Stagnation Test 


This test shall be done to check stagnation temp when 
there is no flow. Place the system with no flow inside 
the receiver. Temperature is measured in stagnant air 
inside the receiver tube. The temperature shall be 
measured at the both ends of receiver tubes and the 
sensors shall not contact the wall. A 50 mm thick thermal 
insulation shall be used at the open ends of the receiver. 


7.2.1 Test Procedure 


When the solar radiance is G > 600 W/m’, record the 
solar irradiance, temperature inside the receiver tube 
and ambient temperature every 5 min. Record the 
temperature inside the receiver by taking average of 
readings from both sensors. Stop the test when 
temperature inside the receiver tube reached a quasi 
steady state. The steady state conditions shall be defined 
as 10 min period when; 


a) variation in receiver tube temperature is + 1°C. 


b) variation in solar radiation is + 20W/m?. 


c) variation in ambient temperature is + 0.2°C. 
d) solar radiation is greater than 600 W/m’. 


Record the quasi steady state temperature as stagnation 
temperature of the system. 


8 THERMAL EFFICIENCY TEST 


8.1 Test Method 


IS 16648 (Part 5) will be used for conducting the 
thermal efficiency test. The collector is mounted on a 
test bay at test centre and hot water or thermic fluid is 
passed through the collector under conditions defined 
in IS 16648 (Part 5) to arrive at thermal efficiency. 


8.2 Acceptance Criteria 


The performance is governed by equation given below. 
NIC is a non-tracking concentrating solar thermal 
technology. Compound parabolic collector works with 
global irradiance. The performance of the system can 
be expressed by following equation:

that location.

8.3 Time Constant 


The NIC shall be subjected to thermal test for 
determination effective thermal capacity and time 
constant in accordance with 6.5 of IS 12933 (Part 5). 
The value of time constant shall be reported alongwith 
test condition for guidance. 


The heat transfer fluid is circulated through the collector 
and the inlet temperature is adjusted as close to ambient 
temperature as possible, preferably within +1°C. The 
steady state and test conditions are maintain as specified 
in IS 16648 (Part 2). The incident solar energy shall be 
then abruptly reduced to zero by using white opaque 
cover. The cover shall be suspended off in such way that 
ambient air is allowed to pass freely over the collector 
surface as prior to the use of cover. The following 
parameters should be measured during the test: 


a) Collector fluid inlet temperature, 
b) Collector fluid outlet temperature, and 
c) Surrounding air temperature. 


The measurements are continue until, 


(T= TT) T;) <0.3

entering the receiver

leaving receiver at the beginning of time 
constant test period, °C.

The value of time constant shall be noted. 


The actual time constant is the time required for the 
quantity on left hand side of equation to change from 
1.0 to 0.368. 


8.4 Incident Angle Modifier 


The solar collector shall be subjected to thermal tests 
for determining incident angle modifier using either of 
the two methods given in 6.6 of IS 12933 (Part 5). The 
value of incident angle modifier shall be reported along 
with graphical presentation given in Fig. 6. 


9 INSTRUCTION MANUAL 


The manufacturer shall provide with collector an 
instruction manual containing schematic diagram of 
collector; recommended diagram of the system; 
installation procedure, startup and shut down 
procedure. The safety instructions during installation 
and operation shall be included in the manual. The 
process of repair, replacement of parts such as broken 
glass tube, peeling of paint and the prevention method 
shall be mentioned in the instruction manual. The service 
outlet with contact details shall be given in the manual.

10.1 The lot shall be supplied with document 
containing: 
a) Manufacturer name, address and contact 
details; 


b) Batch or Lot number with date of 
manufacture; 


c) Maximum working pressure and temperature; 


d) The performance graph and values of a, and 
a, with performance equation as per 8.2; and

10.2 BIS Certification Marking 


Each non-imaging concentrator may also be marked 
with the Standard Mark. 


10.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provision of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
2016 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 


The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


11 PACKING 


The packing shall be as agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 04 (11240).
